title: Trump Retweets White Supremacist Black Crime Statistics (2015)
description_short: Trump Retweets White Supremacist Black Crime Statistics (2015)
description_medium: In November 2015, Trump retweeted a graphic presenting fabricated crime figures. It claimed Black perpetrators caused 81% of white homicide victims’ deaths, a figure far above FBI data. The graphic cited a supposed crime-statistics organization that did not exist, raising questions about the figures’ authenticity and accuracy.
description_long: In November 2015, Trump retweeted a graphic presenting fabricated crime figures that attributed an exceptionally high share of white homicide victims’ deaths to Black perpetrators. FBI data showed a substantially different pattern. The graphic purported to rely on a crime-statistics organization that did not exist, raising questions about the figures’ authenticity as well as their accuracy. Sharing the image from a major presidential candidate’s account extended its audience and made it part of a broader debate about racial messaging during the campaign. The incident is best understood as amplification of false figures; it does not establish that the fictional organization possessed valid data or explain the motives of every person who reposted the image. Its significance lies in the discrepancy between the promoted racial narrative and actual crime records, and in the reach of statistical claims repeated by a national campaign.

title: Facebook and Instagram Suspend Trump Indefinitely
description_short: Facebook and Instagram blocked Trump from posting indefinitely after the Capitol attack, citing risks to public safety.
description_medium: Facebook and Instagram blocked Donald Trump from posting after the January 6 Capitol attack, citing risks to public safety. The companies' decision limited his access to two major channels during the immediate aftermath. The restriction was a platform moderation action, separate from any government order or criminal case.
description_long: Facebook and Instagram blocked Donald Trump from posting after the January 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol, citing risks to public safety. The companies said his posts could contribute to further violence during a period of heightened danger and uncertainty about the transfer of presidential power. The action removed his access to two major social media platforms in the immediate aftermath of the attack. It was taken by the companies under their platform policies, not by a court or government agency, and was separate from criminal investigations or proceedings. The suspension became a prominent example of a technology company restricting the account of a sitting president. The action temporarily limited his ability to communicate with supporters through those two services.
notes: This item covers the initial suspension; the later review and reinstatement terms are a separate event.

title: NYC Property Tax Bribery Scheme and Assessment Fraud
description_short: NYC Property Tax Bribery Scheme and Assessment Fraud
description_medium: Former New York City assessors told ProPublica that Trump’s company used intermediaries to pay bribes and lower property-tax assessments. Their allegations arose from a wider city assessment scandal involving multiple assessors. The reporting did not establish that Trump was convicted of bribery. They concerned alleged payments through intermediaries.
description_long: Donald Trump's organization paid systematic bribes through middlemen to New York City tax assessors to fraudulently reduce property tax assessments on multiple Manhattan buildings, with five former assessors testifying that Trump Organization participated in corruption scheme that collectively stole millions from city taxpayers through false property valuations. The comprehensive tax fraud included Trump Organization employees meeting with 'bag men' who delivered cash envelopes to corrupt assessors in exchange for artificially lowered property assessments, with one assessor recalled Trump thinking he 'should be making the assessment changes for free' when more money was requested for fraudulent services. The property tax conspiracy involved systematic participation in citywide corruption where 18 assessors were eventually indicted for taking bribes to lower building valuations, creating organized criminal enterprise that defrauded city government of tax revenue while enriching property owners through systematic assessment manipulation. Trump's bribery scheme violated federal anti-corruption laws by systematically paying government officials to falsify public records while participating in organized criminal enterprise that stole taxpayer money through fraudulent property assessments designed to reduce Trump's tax obligations illegally. The assessment fraud continued for nearly two decades with Trump Organization buildings receiving favorable treatment through systematic bribery that enabled tax avoidance while other property owners paid legitimate assessments, creating competitive advantage through criminal corruption rather than honest business practices. The tax bribery established Trump's systematic approach to government officials and legal obligations, demonstrating willingness to corrupt public servants while participating in organized fraud schemes that stole from taxpayers through systematic bribery and false documentation designed to avoid legitimate tax responsibilities.

title: Terroristic Tenant Harassment Campaign at 100 Central Park South
description_short: Terroristic Tenant Harassment Campaign at 100 Central Park South
description_medium: Reporting described efforts by Donald Trump to remove rent-controlled tenants at 100 Central Park South, including proposals involving homeless residents and disputes over building conditions. Tenants said they faced pressure to leave protected apartments. The reported tactics became part of wider disputes over rent regulation and tenants’ rights.
description_long: Donald Trump conducted a five-year campaign of psychological warfare against rent-controlled tenants at 100 Central Park South, cutting off heat and hot water, hiring spies to gather personal information, moving homeless people into the building to terrorize elderly residents, and filing hundreds of 'nuisance suits' designed to force vulnerable tenants from their homes through systematic harassment and intimidation. The comprehensive tenant terrorization included eliminating building services while refusing to make repairs, creating dangerous and uninhabitable conditions that forced elderly and disabled residents to choose between enduring abuse or abandoning their legally protected housing rights for Trump's financial benefit. The harassment campaign extended to hiring private investigators to surveil tenants' personal lives while filing frivolous lawsuits alleging lease violations, creating legal and financial pressure designed to exhaust tenants' resources and force surrender of rent-controlled apartments worth millions in conversion value. Trump's tenant persecution violated housing laws and constitutional protections by using economic coercion and psychological abuse to override legal tenant protections, demonstrating systematic willingness to torture vulnerable people for profit while circumventing legal safeguards through intimidation rather than lawful eviction procedures. The terroristic harassment created lasting trauma for elderly tenants who described Trump as wanting 'to be Jesus, to be Hitler, to be the most powerful thing in the world' while systematically disrupting their lives through deliberate cruelty designed to generate real estate profits through human suffering. The tenant warfare established Trump's foundational approach to legal obstacles and vulnerable populations, demonstrating systematic willingness to use psychological torture and illegal harassment to achieve financial goals while causing deliberate harm to people who lacked resources to resist his systematic abuse campaign.

title: Senate Acquits Trump
description_medium: The Senate acquitted Trump on both articles in his first impeachment trial, largely along party lines. Mitt Romney was the only Republican senator to vote for conviction. The outcome prevented removal through that trial, but an acquittal vote should be distinguished from a finding that every allegation was disproved or that later political consequences were inevitable.
description_long: The Republican-led Senate acquitted Trump on both articles in his first impeachment trial. Voting largely followed party lines, with Senator Mitt Romney the sole Republican to vote for conviction. The result meant Trump was not removed from office through that trial. The Senate’s acquittal resolved the charges before it, but did not settle every political or legal question about Trump’s conduct. An acquittal vote does not, by itself, demonstrate that all disputed conduct was disproved, just as a partisan division does not establish every senator's private motivation. The event marked the Senate's resolution of the first trial rather than the end of every political or legal question surrounding Trump's conduct. The supported account preserves the two acquittals and Romney's distinctive vote while keeping later interpretations separate from the documented decision.
notes: The Senate vote and Romney’s dissenting vote are established; a fuller account of the trial evidence and article-specific arguments is needed for context.

title: posts on Truth Social that Canada used AI for a television ad
description_short: posts on Truth Social that Canada used AI for a television ad
description_medium: President Trump posts on Truth Social that Canada used AI for a television ad that used audio from a 1987 address of President Ronald Reagan denouncing tariffs. The Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute later recommended everyone to watch the full unedited address on the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library YouTube account
description_long: In October 2025, Trump posted on Truth Social that Canada had used artificial intelligence in a television advertisement featuring Ronald Reagan’s criticism of tariffs. The advertisement used audio from a 1987 Reagan address opposing tariffs. The Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and Institute urged people to watch the complete, unedited speech. The Foundation’s recommendation documented the source of the audio but did not establish that artificial intelligence generated the advertisement. The dispute unfolded as Trump threatened additional tariffs on Canadian goods and the White House ended trade talks with Canada after the ad aired. Trump’s statement was a public accusation, not proof of how the advertisement was produced. The episode brought a former Republican president’s trade views into a current dispute over U.S.-Canada commerce and showed how statements about media content became part of the escalating trade disagreement.
notes: The ad uses audio from Reagan’s 1987 speech; evidence that AI generated the advertisement is still needed.

title: DOGE Accessed Competitors' Trade Secrets via Federal Data Systems
description_short: DOGE Accessed Competitors' Trade Secrets via Federal Data Systems
description_medium: A Washington Post investigation published June 30, 2025 found that DOGE secured viewing access to sensitive records in at least seven major federal departments containing competitors' trade secrets, nonpublic government contract details, and sensitive regulatory information. Competitors in industries overlapping Musk's empire — including AI, space, and medical devices — were alarmed about potential exposure. The Post found no conflict-of-interest waiver was ever obtained by Musk for any of these access grants.
description_long: A Washington Post investigation published June 30, 2025 reported that the Department of Government Efficiency had viewing access to sensitive records in at least seven federal departments. The materials included government-contract information and regulatory records, some concerning businesses that competed with companies linked to Elon Musk. The reporting described concern among businesses in artificial intelligence, space and medical-device sectors about how the information might be handled. It also said Musk had not received a conflict-of-interest waiver for the access grants. Such access can create a potential conflict when an official has private commercial interests in related fields, but it does not by itself prove that Musk copied or shared information or used it against competitors. The investigation documented access and raised oversight questions; it did not report a final finding of trade-secret theft or data misuse. Federal access to sensitive records can raise oversight concerns when officials have private interests in related industries.

title: Big Beautiful Bill Eliminates Financial Incentive for States to Expand Medicaid
description_short: Big Beautiful Bill Eliminates Financial Incentive for States to Expand Medicaid
description_medium: P.L. 119-21 eliminated the financial incentive under which states that newly adopted ACA Medicaid expansion received a five-percentage-point increase in their FMAP for two years. Ten states had still not expanded Medicaid as of mid-2025; advocates warned the bill's combination of removing expansion incentives and penalizing states for covering immigrant children made it economically irrational for any non-expansion state to newly adopt expansion. CBO estimated the cumulative effect of all anti-expansion provisions would reduce enrollment by millions more than other provisions alone.
description_long: P.L. 119-21 removed the financial incentive that gave states newly adopting Affordable Care Act Medicaid expansion a five-percentage-point increase in their federal matching rate for two years. Ten states had not expanded Medicaid as of mid-2025. Removing the incentive changed the financial terms those states would face if they later adopted expansion. Advocates warned that this change, combined with penalties tied to coverage for immigrant children, could make expansion economically unattractive for states that had not yet adopted it. That was an assessment of likely state decisions, not proof that every state would make the same choice. The Congressional Budget Office estimated that the law’s anti-expansion provisions together would reduce enrollment by millions beyond the effects of other provisions alone. That projection covered the combined provisions, not the incentive change in isolation. The law’s effect on state decisions and enrollment would depend on the remaining provisions and subsequent choices by state governments.
